# Matched execution speedup for the early-stopping baseline and dropout

The user authorized speeding up both jobs, including stopping the recently
started baseline and checking the code for unnecessary work. The replacements
start from seed 0 in fresh directories; previous outputs and source are retained.
The statistical protocol is unchanged: fold 0, 208/52 cases, Dice, AdamW 1e-4,
weight decay 1e-5, StepLR 20/0.5, batch 1, AMP, early stopping 8/0.0005/min25,
maximum 50 epochs, best raw validation Dice selection. Dropout is 0 versus 0.1.

## Root cause

The unconditional zero-loss initializer in `NewConstraintObjective.forward` used
`logits.float().reshape(-1)[0] * 0.0`. The flattened MONAI MetaTensor retained its
batch flag, so indexing triggered metadata decollation across 786,432 elements.
This ran even for `constraint_set=none`. In an eight-batch CPU profile it consumed
86.664 of 89.181 seconds (profiler overhead included), with 6.29 million metadata
handling calls. This is accidental overhead, not constraint computation.

The fix obtains a plain tensor view before scalar indexing, preserving the exact
zero expression and its autograd connection. A regression test rejects any
decollation in this code path and verifies zero gradients on the original tensor.

## Other measured changes

- Both runs discard metadata only after identical preprocessing. Case names and
  voxel values are preserved; the model and losses do not use affine metadata.
- Disable activation recomputation. This changes execution memory/computation,
  not the architecture or dropout masks. The original CUDA microbenchmark found
  80.8/82.8 ms forward/backward for baseline/dropout versus 47.6/48.0 ms with both
  optimizations, at peak allocated memory 1.43/1.44 GB. Identical outputs, losses,
  and the checked parameter gradient were observed for both dropout settings.
- Keep batch size, precision, deterministic settings, validation frequency,
  diagnostics, checkpoint durability, and zero data-loader workers unchanged.
- Print train/validation/checkpoint/total seconds after each durable epoch.
- Perform the shared best/latest train/validation audit after the dropout job,
  avoiding a historical-model audit delaying its start. Both new runs are audited.

Other measured costs on the A100 MIG allocation: data loading approximately
8–13 ms/batch, optimizer updates 4 ms after warmup, checkpoint write 0.59 s for
196 MB, source hashing 0.25 s. Validation diagnostics on plain tensors took about
8 ms/case versus 20 ms for metadata tensors after warmup. Library imports took
83 s in the instrumented process: a startup cost, not a per-batch delay.

The profile records are `loop_profile.log`, `loop_profile.profile.txt`, and
`speed_benchmark.json`. A complete fast epoch is run before job replacement to
measure actual throughput and compare metrics to the saved original epoch 1.

## Execution and artifacts

Cluster root: `/mnt/beegfsstudents/home/3160552/regularization_fast_20260916_01`.
Separate baseline and dropout jobs, each one 4g.40gb GPU, six CPUs, 64 GB, 24 h.
Dropout depends on successful completion of the replacement baseline. Source
and run hashes remain strict; old checkpoints are not relabeled as new runs.
The final audit compares best/latest from both runs with dropout off and the
same preprocessing, tensor representation, CUDA/AMP, and error normalization.

Evidence of compute/memory tradeoff:

# Scalar-presence feasibility diagnostic

Added after the first component fold showed that setting true-thin presence to
one recovers correct anatomy but adds FP voxels within occupied rays. This is a
post-hoc mechanistic follow-up, not a modification of the already running
capacity/pooling experiment or its selection rules.

Question: can ANY increase of a ray's scalar presence recover its true thin
voxels without also activating wrong voxels, with raw logits and fitted edges
fixed? A larger classifier cannot overcome an infeasible per-ray ordering.

On every true thin ray, find the smallest increase of log presence that achieves
(a) at least one correct foreground voxel, and separately (b) every true
foreground voxel. Use 24 vectorized bisection steps between original log
presence and zero (presence one); only attempt rays for which presence one can
achieve the endpoint. Leave all other rays exactly unchanged. Ray endpoints
are monotone because the foreground margin increases monotonically with
presence and anterior/posterior logits stay unchanged.

Report target rays, feasible rays, recovered correct voxels, additional FP
voxels on those same rays, number of recoveries with zero extra FP voxels,
whole-mask ASSD/overlap, and distribution of required presence. Validate the
bisection endpoints and guarantee that empty rays are bitwise unchanged.
Count residual unrecoverable cases separately. All variants use reference
labels and are non-deployable. This measures conditional representational
feasibility, not whether a learned network can choose these values or achieve
the outcome on new data.

The minimum required presence need not be a calibrated existence probability.
If near-one classification induces overshoot but minimal increases avoid it,
decoupling existence probability from correction strength is a more specific
next hypothesis than simply widening the head.

# Presence mechanism: frozen development experiments

Status: specified before new checkpoint inference or training. These are internal
mechanism experiments on the reused MSD pool, not independent confirmation.
Existing A/D/E checkpoints and historical reports must never be overwritten.

## Stage 1: component interventions and surface attribution

Evaluate all 208 outer cases from folds 1–4 using saved A and E checkpoints.
Verify each checkpoint against its done.json hash, dataset/split hashes, and
reproduce the saved case-level ASSD before accepting any new results.

Prespecified E interventions: raw output; original renderer; oracle presence in
the renderer only with fitted edges fixed; oracle edges on true rays with
presence fixed; both; oracle presence in the fit only; oracle presence in fit
and renderer; unit presence only on true thin rays; edge distribution moments
without fitting; interval-distance occupancy with all predictions fixed; restore
raw masks on erased true thin rays; reference-mask replacement on missed thin,
missed thicker, empty false-positive, and present-but-wrong true rays separately.
Every intervention using reference labels is explicitly non-deployable.

Primary mechanistic outcomes: correctly overlapping thin-ray recall, thin voxel
recall, and directional ASSD contributions. Ray presence alone is insufficient.
Record empty-ray FPs, FP voxels/components, signed volume error, class/union Dice,
HD95, all-present and conditional edge MAE, and raw/rendered decision margins.
Thin means a contiguous reference interval of span 1 or 2; two disconnected
voxels are multi-run, not thin. Report border rays separately.

Partition surface contributions into empty, thin length 1, thin length 2,
length 3–5, length >=6, multi-run, and border rays. Subdivide true rays using
the original E final presence decision, fixed for every compared output.
Contributions use each method's own prediction-surface denominator and the
common reference-surface denominator, and must sum to its original ASSD.
Also report fixed-reference coverage at 0, 1, and 2 mm. Counterfactual effects
are nonadditive; they are not achievable bounds or proof of learnability.

## Stage 2: capacity versus pooling, conditional on the saved E representation

Four arms form a 2x2 comparison: width 24 or 48, with duplicated-mean pooling
or mean-plus-max pooling. Every arm is a dedicated trainable presence stem
cloned from E; the backbone, feature projection, edge distributions, fitted
edges, renderer temperature, and beta remain frozen. Presence changes only the
renderer. Thus this stage isolates classification from geometry co-adaptation.

The presence output convolution receives 2*width channels in every arm. Its
first half is initialized from E; the second half is zero. The mean control
duplicates the mean features, matching parameter count to mean-plus-max.
Width 48 uses function-preserving channel duplication with cancelling output
perturbations to break duplicate-channel gradient symmetry. Assert identical
initial presence and final masks for all arms against E.

Train all arms for 12 epochs, AdamW lr=1e-4, weight_decay=1e-5, batch size one
volume. Seeds 0, 1, 2 determine paired case order and symmetry-breaking noise.
Use E's 166 fitting cases; its 42 inner cases select checkpoints; the 52 outer
cases are processed only after all arm/seed selections for that fold are fixed.
The fitting data previously trained E: this is explicitly conditional on E and
may contain in-sample feature optimism. These are presence-training seeds, not
independent backbone-training seeds.

Loss: equal mean BCE over four nonempty groups per case: true thin rays,
other true rays, hard empty rays, and other empty rays. Hard empty means raw E
has any positive argmax voxel OR original E head presence >=0.5. All empty rays
receive supervision. Freeze groups from original E/reference labels; no outer
label-dependent feature construction or selection. No focal-weight grid.

At epochs 0, 4, 8, 12, evaluate unshifted head probabilities and the prespecified
presence-logit offsets -1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1 on inner validation only. Include
unchanged E as a fallback. Select maximum case-mean correctly overlapping
thin-ray recall subject to mean FP rays and total FP voxels <= E, mean thin
voxel recall >= E, and ASSD <= E+0.002 mm. Break ties by lower ASSD, then lower
FP rays, earlier epoch, smaller absolute offset. The 0.002 mm margin is a
development guard, not a clinical noninferiority margin. Also save unconstrained
training/inner losses and epoch-zero metrics to distinguish optimization
failure, overfitting, and failure of the operating constraint.

Report selected and final uncalibrated heads, not just fallback-selected output.
Primary contrasts are width48-minus-width24 within each pooling strategy and
max-minus-mean at each width. Report all folds/seeds, paired case changes after
averaging seeds, and seed-to-seed variability separately. Do not count seeds or
rays as independent patients. A null result is evidence about this intervention,
not a proof that arbitrary larger end-to-end heads cannot help.

## Decision rules and next stage

If oracle renderer presence does not restore correct thin anatomy, do not
interpret more capacity as the primary remedy. If it restores anatomy but
larger heads do not improve held-out FP-matched preservation, capacity at these
widths is unsupported. A pooling advantage with no width advantage favors an
evidence-aggregation bottleneck. Improvements confined to fitting cases favor
overfitting; universal no-op selection requires inspecting unselected metrics.

Only a clear capacity/pooling improvement proceeds to matched end-to-end
training with independent backbone seeds. A separate three-arm gradient study
(D-prime, rendered loss with detached geometry, full E) remains a subsequent
experiment; this frozen-head study cannot answer that question.

No automatic promotion, external generalization claim, clinical claim, pruning
of previous checkpoints, or modification of historical primary results.

## Reproduction amendment before component results were available

Job 666639 stopped at the 1e-4 mm case-level reproduction guard on fold 1,
hippocampus_166. The original record is 0.3497679963 mm; multiple existing
read-only re-evaluations give 0.3504276702 mm. REFERENCE_E.csv is frozen from
the previously saved raw-thin-rescue baseline, with source/hash in its provenance
JSON. The rerun checks E against this previously recorded re-evaluation at the
same 1e-4 tolerance and records BOTH old and repeated references. A is still
checked against the original record. All treatment comparisons use the current
paired baseline. This is a reproducibility amendment, not a changed scientific
endpoint, selection rule, or intervention. A repeated-inference diagnostic also
compares the old evaluator with the new metric code on the affected case.

# Full-data augmented A/P interface-distance-weighted pilot

This is a seed-0, fold-0 pilot on 208 training and 52 validation cases. It asks
whether concentrating a foreground-conditional original-label A/P logistic CE
near the internal A/P interface helps beyond the same uniform auxiliary. It is
not a global anatomical/order constraint and one seed does not establish
generalization.

The single production Slurm job runs three fresh arms sequentially: augmented
Dice; augmented Dice plus uniform conditional A/P CE; and augmented Dice plus
interface-distance-weighted conditional A/P CE. All use the same SwinUNETR,
Dice implementation, seed, data order, mild_v1 RNG stream, AdamW (1e-4,
weight decay 1e-5), StepLR (20, 0.5), AMP, batch size one, and identity-input
validation. Maximum training is 80 epochs, minimum 50, patience 12, and
meaningful-improvement delta 0.0005. Best checkpoints retain every strict Dice
improvement; latest is the explicit final/stopping checkpoint.

The interface contains both voxels of every face-sharing 1/2 contact in the
original or transformed released label. Foreground/background contacts do not
belong to it. R is the literal maximum Euclidean processed-grid distance from
any fold-0 training foreground voxel to that interface, after a 208-case
inventory is inspected. Validation labels never contribute. Weighted CE uses
`w = 1 + 4 * max(0, 1 - d/R)^2`, normalized by the sum of weights per valid
case. After accepted isotropic augmentation, `d_effective = d_aug / scale`;
identity, nonspatial, and rejected transforms use scale one. Absent interfaces
are explicitly invalid and never receive manufactured distances.

Both auxiliary coefficients are calibrated independently from the same
predeclared fresh baseline epoch-10 checkpoint and the same deterministic
32-training-case mild_v1 panel. The chosen coefficient is the smaller of the
weight matching the median auxiliary output-logit gradient RMS to 10% of the
median Dice RMS and the weight capping the auxiliary 95th-percentile RMS at
50% of the median Dice RMS. Calibration has a dedicated RNG and occurs before
either candidate is optimized.

The bounded GPU preflight runs analytic/augmentation/schedule tests, inventories
R, verifies the real data/model path, and measures full update, EDT, CPU/GPU
transfer, and checkpoint costs. Production ordinary updates use one network
forward. Maximum production optimizer updates are 49,920.

Best/final post-hoc diagnostics cover identity training and validation plus one
fixed augmented training view per case: class Dice, FP/FN, A-to-P and P-to-A,
raw conditional A/P errors on all GT foreground, distance-stratified swaps, and
cut fits only for axis-aligned views. Rotated-view cut geometry is explicitly
unmeasured. Only identity validation hard Dice selects checkpoints; matched
epoch curves are descriptive.

# Raw-backbone endpoint auxiliary screen — locked 2026-09-23

## Question and scope

Does explicit endpoint supervision improve raw three-class SwinUNETR, and does
additional actual-label completion help? This is a new auxiliary architecture,
not a reproduction of SegFix, PointRend, the prior renderer or a proven benefit.
The final inference operation is backbone(image).argmax(1). No rendering,
presence head, predicted interval fill, or labels enter inference.

Four folds (1–4), each 166 fitting / 42 inner / 52 outer; 208 distinct outer
cases from the same 260-case reused internal development pool. Original A
backbones have training seed 0. Continuation RNG is 3401 + fold, with explicit
matched epoch data seeds 3401 + fold + 1000 + epoch. Fold variation and head
randomness are not backbone-seed replication. This is a bounded screen;
independent backbone seed confirmation would require a separate subsequent run.
No new-cohort or clinical claim. No hyperparameter grid or tuning on outer labels.

## Common start and schedule

Start each fold from verified original A/best.pt of job 666174 (NOT E raw).
Original A optimizer states were pruned; restart AdamW identically, explicitly
making this a continuation experiment with optimizer restart. Backbone AdamW:
3e-5 LR, 1e-5 decay; head AdamW: 1e-3 LR, 1e-5 decay. Constant LR throughout
this short continuation, batch size 2 and the original deterministic dataset
preprocessing. Original runs allowed 50 epochs with early stopping; recent
continuation convention was six epochs at 3e-5. Here no arm stops early.

One shared fitting pass (83 backbone updates) prepares the head on detached
decoder features while the backbone follows original A's Dice+CE expression.
Save paired model, head, both optimizers/scalers, all RNGs and counters together.
All three branches restore that same state. Then six fitting passes per arm:
498 matched branch updates, 581 backbone updates including preparation.
The preparation pass is an initialization budget, NOT an anatomy readiness
threshold. Existing A provides established segmentation; per-batch actual
overlap is the sole activation/readiness rule. We make no evidence-based claim
that one pass makes the head accurate enough; head errors and raw outcomes test it.
No loss plateau, fixed 21–25 epoch activation, or inner/outer readiness tuning.

Arms: control (Dice+CE; head stays detached), endpoint (Dice+CE + endpoint
feature gradient), endpoint_completion (same + raw-voxel completion). The
completion coefficient is the ONLY prescribed difference between the two
auxiliary arms. Moving predictions naturally make their later eligibility differ.

## Representation, labels and routing

Input is the full 24-channel last decoder tensor captured before backbone.out,
over full 64-voxel z columns; no predicted crop, four-channel compression,
probability input, GT input or endpoint anchoring. Head: Conv3d(24,24,3,pad=1),
GELU, Conv3d(24,24,3,pad=1), GELU, Conv3d(24,2,1). 31,202 parameters. Local
5x5x5 receptive field, neighboring x/y context, two independent full-column
softmax distributions over z. No normalization couples ray statistics.
This small local score network does not claim global anatomical context beyond
the backbone representation and full-column softmax competition.

Endpoint target: first/last true foreground index. Exclude empty rays, rays
touching either z boundary, and true multi-run rays from endpoint supervision.
Log all exclusions, missed thin rays and actual overlapping ray counts.
Head optimizer always learns from ALL true geometrically valid fitting rays,
including rays the backbone misses, using features.detach().

Backbone endpoint loss is mean first/last categorical CE over geometrically
valid rays with at least one raw argmax foreground voxel at a TRUE foreground
position. Argmax and eligibility are detached. Mere wrong-location presence
does not qualify. A separate head forward uses detached head parameters;
feature gradients are masked at the input ray AND loss output ray, so a
noneligible neighbor supplies context but receives no direct feature gradient.
The head fit has no path to logits/backbone. Shared upstream parameters can
still change noneligible predictions; gating does NOT guarantee preservation.

Completion uses ALL true overlapping rays (including truncated and multi-run
rays since voxel labels remain valid). For each ray, separately mean three-class
CE over true foreground and actual background, equally average the nonempty
groups, then mean rays. Includes background gaps and surrounding background.
No endpoint-derived voxel targets. Zero eligible rays give differentiable zero;
missing foreground/background groups are omitted without NaNs. Whole-volume
Dice+CE continues to supervise missed rays and empty-ray FPs in every arm.

## Weights fixed by fitting-only calibration

After shared preparation, use exactly the first four fitting batches, FP32,
without optimizer updates; restore RNG afterward. Endpoint coefficient is 0.1
times median Dice+CE decoder-feature gradient RMS divided by median endpoint
decoder-feature gradient RMS. Completion coefficient uses the analogous ratio
at raw logits. The 0.1 target follows the existing calibration convention; its
suitability for this new task is NOT established. Fail if coefficient is nonfinite
or outside [1e-6,10], do not silently clip or tune. Freeze numerical coefficients
once per fold before branches. Ramp both auxiliary coefficients from 1/83 to
1 across the first continuation pass; thereafter constant. This ramp is an
optimization precaution, not a learned/readiness threshold. Head fit weight is
1 in its separate optimizer and has no effect on baseline AMP scaling/skips.

## Evaluation and selection locked before submission

Evaluate raw predictions only. Head endpoint MAE is diagnostic, never a selection
criterion. Inner metrics every epoch: ASSD (1 mm), union and class Dice, actual
thin overlap recall, thin voxel recall, FP rays/voxels, core recall (one 3D
binary erosion), true-voxel deletion/recovery relative to shared start and
matched control epoch, and endpoint errors/exclusion counts. Historical thin
recall definition is nonborder true span <=2; deletion audit additionally uses
one/two true voxels regardless of span. Keep these definitions explicit.

Control candidates must preserve shared-start Dice, both thin recalls, core
recall, FP rays and FP voxels (no worsening). Require zero newly deleted core
and count-thin true voxels, and total true deletions <= true recoveries.
Auxiliary candidates must satisfy these same guards against BOTH shared start
and the SAME-EPOCH control, and strictly improve ASSD against each. Select
minimum inner ASSD among eligible epochs; retain epoch 0 if none qualify.
These intentionally strict guards may reject every checkpoint. No post-hoc
relaxation. Fixed epoch-six results for all arms remain the main matched-update
comparison regardless of guard failure. Selected results are separately labeled
and may have different update counts; do not conflate them with fixed-epoch results.

Outer labels only compute reports after fixed training and inner selection;
they never change optimization, weights, readiness, selection or next fold's
settings. Report both fixed epoch-six and separately selected outcomes. Mask
banks used for paired deletion audits stay on cluster, with split/case records.
Only non-identifying aggregate JSON and job/test metadata may be downloaded.

## Integrity, storage and execution

Check dataset, split, original A checkpoints against recorded hashes, and frozen
source against provenance of job 666651. Record experiment/protocol hashes,
library version, argument settings and exact head parameter count. Resume checks
configuration and arm weights, restores paired state/RNG/counters, and skips
completed arms. Epoch snapshots are atomic. Training restarts from last complete
epoch after interruption, with deterministic matched data order. Never create a
second scheduler job to resume while the original is active.
CUDA deterministic algorithms use warn-only mode because cluster PyTorch 2.12
has no deterministic implementation of the original mean cross-entropy
reduction. Keep that original loss, fixed seeds and deterministic cuDNN; do not
claim every CUDA operation is bitwise deterministic. The real-batch preparation
parity assertion still requires exact weights and AdamW moments.

Local tests: overlap rejects wrong position; all detachment paths; contextual
gradient masking; completion sign/gaps/empty groups; baseline optimizer parity;
zero completion arm equivalence; state/RNG restore; raw-only evaluation.
GPU smoke: two real preparation updates, exact weight/AdamW parity with pure
baseline, four-batch calibration, two active updates, paired checkpoint reload.
Run GPU smoke before submitting full training. Smoke is not experiment evidence.

Resource request: stud, one gpu:4g.40gb, 8 CPUs, 32 GiB RAM; smoke 20 minutes,
screen 4 hours. Estimated persistent experiment checkpoints approximately 4 GiB,
plus small mask banks; current free quota ~8.15 GiB. Require 2 GiB quota reserve
before each checkpoint write. No cleanup needed at lock time. If quota later
blocks, only user-authorized completed disposable artifacts may be considered
after provenance/scheduler/symlink checks; no automatic blanket cleanup.

Protocol evidence: correction_discrimination_20260923_01a0cd/CORRECTION_DISCRIMINATION_PROTOCOL_20260923.md
# Saved-head discrimination audit

Written before running this diagnostic. This is a retrospective audit of the
24 final, unselected heads from job 666769, not a new model-selection experiment.

Use all 166 fitting and 42 inner cases in each original fold. Evaluate both
objectives and all three head-fitting seeds. No outer images, weight updates,
checkpoint reselection or changes to the completed experiment are allowed.

For true thin rays, other true rays, hard-empty rays, other empty rays, and
feasible initially missed thin rays, record the distribution of learned
renderer-control corrections: count, mean, standard deviation and quantiles.
Compute within-case AUROC for thin versus hard-empty and feasible missed thin
versus hard-empty using correction alone, original anchor, and final control.
Average defined case AUCs; report distributions within each fold/seed rather
than treating overlapping fitting folds as independent patients. Constant
corrections have AUC 0.5 whenever both groups exist.

Recompute label-dependent feasible intervals on fitting and inner data solely
as retrospective diagnostics. Inner reference intervals never enter fitting,
constant selection, optimizer steps, or model inputs. Their availability at
audit time does not make them deployable targets or inference features.

Compare the learned correction with E and two constants chosen using fitting
data only: the case-averaged learned correction, and the constant in [-4,4]
minimizing the arm's original case/group-balanced fitting objective. Include
the endpoints and zero in constant minimization. Apply the same constants to
inner data, without re-estimating them there. Compare fitting objective values,
mask disagreement, true-voxel recoveries/deletions, thin overlap/voxel recall,
FP rays and FP voxels. ASSD is not recomputed for this discrimination diagnostic.

Interpretations to test:

- Near-constant corrections, chance ranking and similar constant-mask outcomes
  on fitting data undermine a pure held-out generalization explanation.
- Good fitting discrimination with poor inner discrimination suggests a
  generalization problem.
- Useful ranking but worse-than-constant voxel outcomes suggests that correction
  amplitude or renderer activation thresholds defeat the apparent ranking.
- Lower fitting loss than the best constant establishes input-dependent benefit
  for that objective; it does not establish selective anatomical rescue.

If fitting discrimination is poor, optimization and representational limits
remain unresolved until a small controlled overfit/feature-access experiment.
No architecture change is inferred automatically from a low AUC.

Record saved checkpoint/source/data/split hashes and no-gradient assertions.
Write only aggregates from this audit; individual diagnostic records and image
data must not be exported. Report all 24 heads, including null findings.

# Frozen-head loss, activation and gradient audit

Written before execution. Audit the 24 final heads of job 666786 on exactly
their four fitting cases per fold (seven distinct cases across folds). No
training, checkpoint reselection, inner or outer evaluation.

Decompose the original case/group-balanced interval objective exactly into six
disjoint groups: initially missed feasible thin rays, initially missed infeasible
thin rays, initially overlapping thin rays, other true rays, hard-empty rays,
and other empty rays. Preserve original four-group normalization; splitting a
group for reporting must not increase its loss weight. Split each contribution
into lower hinge, upper hinge, tie and infeasible-zero terms. Assert the losses
and parameter gradients sum back to the unchanged original objective. Compare
paired state-input versus original-input contributions and zero-correction loss.

For currently unrescued feasible thin rays, report distance in residual logits
to the safe rescue lower bound, allowed interval width and the derivative of the
bounded tanh correction. Report fractions of gaps within .01,.1,.25,.5,1,2 logits.
These label-defined measurements are retrospective diagnostics, not features.

Report actual masks for unchanged learned corrections and fixed +0.25/+0.5-logit
increments, clipped to the original domain. Also evaluate a explicitly
non-deployable oracle: increase only currently unrescued feasible true thin rays
to their target lower bound, leaving every other learned correction unchanged.
Assert that this oracle adds no FP voxel or true deletion relative to the learned
mask. It quantifies available selective rescue, not a deployable result or the
share of total ASSD attributable to thin rays. No ASSD is recomputed.

At each saved head, compute gradients for each weighted group contribution,
their norms and pairwise cosines. Compute derivatives of the mean correction
on currently unrescued feasible thin rays, hard-empty rays and already-overlapping
thin rays, pooling each receiver's rays over the four cases. Report the signed
first-order response to minus the total gradient normalized to unit parameter
L2 norm, and each loss group's additive contribution to that same direction.
Positive response means increased mean correction. Direct loss gradients with
respect to correction are reported separately. This is a local SGD diagnostic,
not an AdamW update, historical causal reconstruction or training forecast.
Saved optimizer states are not available and no parameter update is performed.

Numerical amendment after job 666811 stopped on a componentwise float32
gradient check: record reconstruction L2 error relative to the sum of subgroup
norms and the total norm. Require error <= 1e-5 times subgroup-norm sum + 1e-7.
Use the directly computed original-objective gradient for the total direction;
suppress signed responses if its norm is not at least ten times reconstruction
error. Record maximum absolute error as well. This changes diagnostic numerical
validation only, not model weights, loss definitions or subgroup weighting.

Discriminating findings:

- Concentrated loss reduction on feasible missed thin rays supports improvement
  on the intended target, but must be checked against actual threshold crossings.
- Small gaps with unsaturated correction suggest threshold placement is an
  actionable issue; large gaps refute a merely numerical near-threshold account.
- Opposing group gradients and adverse shared-parameter response despite the
  desired direct output signal support local gradient interference.
- Saturation, zero gradients or missing signal suggest different mechanisms.
  None alone establishes the cause of earlier training failures.

Report all heads, paired fold/seed differences and heterogeneous signs. Verify
source/input/checkpoint hashes and reproduce saved fitting losses. Export only
non-identifying aggregates under the user's authorization for current and future
aggregate reports in this investigation. Keep images and individual case records
on the cluster; preserve every saved model.

# Presence mechanism: frozen development experiments

Status: specified before new checkpoint inference or training. These are internal
mechanism experiments on the reused MSD pool, not independent confirmation.
Existing A/D/E checkpoints and historical reports must never be overwritten.

## Stage 1: component interventions and surface attribution

Evaluate all 208 outer cases from folds 1–4 using saved A and E checkpoints.
Verify each checkpoint against its done.json hash, dataset/split hashes, and
reproduce the saved case-level ASSD before accepting any new results.

Prespecified E interventions: raw output; original renderer; oracle presence in
the renderer only with fitted edges fixed; oracle edges on true rays with
presence fixed; both; oracle presence in the fit only; oracle presence in fit
and renderer; unit presence only on true thin rays; edge distribution moments
without fitting; interval-distance occupancy with all predictions fixed; restore
raw masks on erased true thin rays; reference-mask replacement on missed thin,
missed thicker, empty false-positive, and present-but-wrong true rays separately.
Every intervention using reference labels is explicitly non-deployable.

Primary mechanistic outcomes: correctly overlapping thin-ray recall, thin voxel
recall, and directional ASSD contributions. Ray presence alone is insufficient.
Record empty-ray FPs, FP voxels/components, signed volume error, class/union Dice,
HD95, all-present and conditional edge MAE, and raw/rendered decision margins.
Thin means a contiguous reference interval of span 1 or 2; two disconnected
voxels are multi-run, not thin. Report border rays separately.

Partition surface contributions into empty, thin length 1, thin length 2,
length 3–5, length >=6, multi-run, and border rays. Subdivide true rays using
the original E final presence decision, fixed for every compared output.
Contributions use each method's own prediction-surface denominator and the
common reference-surface denominator, and must sum to its original ASSD.
Also report fixed-reference coverage at 0, 1, and 2 mm. Counterfactual effects
are nonadditive; they are not achievable bounds or proof of learnability.

## Stage 2: capacity versus pooling, conditional on the saved E representation

Four arms form a 2x2 comparison: width 24 or 48, with duplicated-mean pooling
or mean-plus-max pooling. Every arm is a dedicated trainable presence stem
cloned from E; the backbone, feature projection, edge distributions, fitted
edges, renderer temperature, and beta remain frozen. Presence changes only the
renderer. Thus this stage isolates classification from geometry co-adaptation.

The presence output convolution receives 2*width channels in every arm. Its
first half is initialized from E; the second half is zero. The mean control
duplicates the mean features, matching parameter count to mean-plus-max.
Width 48 uses function-preserving channel duplication with cancelling output
perturbations to break duplicate-channel gradient symmetry. Assert identical
initial presence and final masks for all arms against E.

Train all arms for 12 epochs, AdamW lr=1e-4, weight_decay=1e-5, batch size one
volume. Seeds 0, 1, 2 determine paired case order and symmetry-breaking noise.
Use E's 166 fitting cases; its 42 inner cases select checkpoints; the 52 outer
cases are processed only after all arm/seed selections for that fold are fixed.
The fitting data previously trained E: this is explicitly conditional on E and
may contain in-sample feature optimism. These are presence-training seeds, not
independent backbone-training seeds.

Loss: equal mean BCE over four nonempty groups per case: true thin rays,
other true rays, hard empty rays, and other empty rays. Hard empty means raw E
has any positive argmax voxel OR original E head presence >=0.5. All empty rays
receive supervision. Freeze groups from original E/reference labels; no outer
label-dependent feature construction or selection. No focal-weight grid.

At epochs 0, 4, 8, 12, evaluate unshifted head probabilities and the prespecified
presence-logit offsets -1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1 on inner validation only. Include
unchanged E as a fallback. Select maximum case-mean correctly overlapping
thin-ray recall subject to mean FP rays and total FP voxels <= E, mean thin
voxel recall >= E, and ASSD <= E+0.002 mm. Break ties by lower ASSD, then lower
FP rays, earlier epoch, smaller absolute offset. The 0.002 mm margin is a
development guard, not a clinical noninferiority margin. Also save unconstrained
training/inner losses and epoch-zero metrics to distinguish optimization
failure, overfitting, and failure of the operating constraint.

Report selected and final uncalibrated heads, not just fallback-selected output.
Primary contrasts are width48-minus-width24 within each pooling strategy and
max-minus-mean at each width. Report all folds/seeds, paired case changes after
averaging seeds, and seed-to-seed variability separately. Do not count seeds or
rays as independent patients. A null result is evidence about this intervention,
not a proof that arbitrary larger end-to-end heads cannot help.

## Decision rules and next stage

If oracle renderer presence does not restore correct thin anatomy, do not
interpret more capacity as the primary remedy. If it restores anatomy but
larger heads do not improve held-out FP-matched preservation, capacity at these
widths is unsupported. A pooling advantage with no width advantage favors an
evidence-aggregation bottleneck. Improvements confined to fitting cases favor
overfitting; universal no-op selection requires inspecting unselected metrics.

Only a clear capacity/pooling improvement proceeds to matched end-to-end
training with independent backbone seeds. A separate three-arm gradient study
(D-prime, rendered loss with detached geometry, full E) remains a subsequent
experiment; this frozen-head study cannot answer that question.

No automatic promotion, external generalization claim, clinical claim, pruning
of previous checkpoints, or modification of historical primary results.

voxel recall >= E, and ASSD <= E+0.002 mm. Break ties by lower ASSD, then lower
FP rays, earlier epoch, smaller absolute offset. The 0.002 mm margin is a
development guard, not a clinical noninferiority margin. Also save unconstrained
training/inner losses and epoch-zero metrics to distinguish optimization
failure, overfitting, and failure of the operating constraint.

Report selected and final uncalibrated heads, not just fallback-selected output.
Primary contrasts are width48-minus-width24 within each pooling strategy and
max-minus-mean at each width. Report all folds/seeds, paired case changes after
averaging seeds, and seed-to-seed variability separately. Do not count seeds or
rays as independent patients. A null result is evidence about this intervention,
not a proof that arbitrary larger end-to-end heads cannot help.

## Decision rules and next stage

If oracle renderer presence does not restore correct thin anatomy, do not
interpret more capacity as the primary remedy. If it restores anatomy but
larger heads do not improve held-out FP-matched preservation, capacity at these
widths is unsupported. A pooling advantage with no width advantage favors an
evidence-aggregation bottleneck. Improvements confined to fitting cases favor
overfitting; universal no-op selection requires inspecting unselected metrics.

Only a clear capacity/pooling improvement proceeds to matched end-to-end
training with independent backbone seeds. A separate three-arm gradient study
(D-prime, rendered loss with detached geometry, full E) remains a subsequent
experiment; this frozen-head study cannot answer that question.

No automatic promotion, external generalization claim, clinical claim, pruning
of previous checkpoints, or modification of historical primary results.

# Raw-backbone endpoint auxiliary screen — locked 2026-09-23

## Question and scope

Does explicit endpoint supervision improve raw three-class SwinUNETR, and does
additional actual-label completion help? This is a new auxiliary architecture,
not a reproduction of SegFix, PointRend, the prior renderer or a proven benefit.
The final inference operation is backbone(image).argmax(1). No rendering,
presence head, predicted interval fill, or labels enter inference.

Four folds (1–4), each 166 fitting / 42 inner / 52 outer; 208 distinct outer
cases from the same 260-case reused internal development pool. Original A
backbones have training seed 0. Continuation RNG is 3401 + fold, with explicit
matched epoch data seeds 3401 + fold + 1000 + epoch. Fold variation and head
randomness are not backbone-seed replication. This is a bounded screen;
independent backbone seed confirmation would require a separate subsequent run.
No new-cohort or clinical claim. No hyperparameter grid or tuning on outer labels.

## Common start and schedule

Start each fold from verified original A/best.pt of job 666174 (NOT E raw).
Original A optimizer states were pruned; restart AdamW identically, explicitly
making this a continuation experiment with optimizer restart. Backbone AdamW:
3e-5 LR, 1e-5 decay; head AdamW: 1e-3 LR, 1e-5 decay. Constant LR throughout
this short continuation, batch size 2 and the original deterministic dataset
preprocessing. Original runs allowed 50 epochs with early stopping; recent
continuation convention was six epochs at 3e-5. Here no arm stops early.

One shared fitting pass (83 backbone updates) prepares the head on detached
decoder features while the backbone follows original A's Dice+CE expression.
Save paired model, head, both optimizers/scalers, all RNGs and counters together.
All three branches restore that same state. Then six fitting passes per arm:
498 matched branch updates, 581 backbone updates including preparation.
The preparation pass is an initialization budget, NOT an anatomy readiness
threshold. Existing A provides established segmentation; per-batch actual
overlap is the sole activation/readiness rule. We make no evidence-based claim
that one pass makes the head accurate enough; head errors and raw outcomes test it.
No loss plateau, fixed 21–25 epoch activation, or inner/outer readiness tuning.

Arms: control (Dice+CE; head stays detached), endpoint (Dice+CE + endpoint
feature gradient), endpoint_completion (same + raw-voxel completion). The
completion coefficient is the ONLY prescribed difference between the two
auxiliary arms. Moving predictions naturally make their later eligibility differ.

## Representation, labels and routing

Input is the full 24-channel last decoder tensor captured before backbone.out,
over full 64-voxel z columns; no predicted crop, four-channel compression,
probability input, GT input or endpoint anchoring. Head: Conv3d(24,24,3,pad=1),
GELU, Conv3d(24,24,3,pad=1), GELU, Conv3d(24,2,1). 31,202 parameters. Local
5x5x5 receptive field, neighboring x/y context, two independent full-column
softmax distributions over z. No normalization couples ray statistics.
This small local score network does not claim global anatomical context beyond
the backbone representation and full-column softmax competition.

Endpoint target: first/last true foreground index. Exclude empty rays, rays
touching either z boundary, and true multi-run rays from endpoint supervision.
Log all exclusions, missed thin rays and actual overlapping ray counts.
Head optimizer always learns from ALL true geometrically valid fitting rays,
including rays the backbone misses, using features.detach().

Backbone endpoint loss is mean first/last categorical CE over geometrically
valid rays with at least one raw argmax foreground voxel at a TRUE foreground
position. Argmax and eligibility are detached. Mere wrong-location presence
does not qualify. A separate head forward uses detached head parameters;
feature gradients are masked at the input ray AND loss output ray, so a
noneligible neighbor supplies context but receives no direct feature gradient.
The head fit has no path to logits/backbone. Shared upstream parameters can
still change noneligible predictions; gating does NOT guarantee preservation.

Completion uses ALL true overlapping rays (including truncated and multi-run
rays since voxel labels remain valid). For each ray, separately mean three-class
CE over true foreground and actual background, equally average the nonempty
groups, then mean rays. Includes background gaps and surrounding background.
No endpoint-derived voxel targets. Zero eligible rays give differentiable zero;
missing foreground/background groups are omitted without NaNs. Whole-volume
Dice+CE continues to supervise missed rays and empty-ray FPs in every arm.

## Weights fixed by fitting-only calibration

After shared preparation, use exactly the first four fitting batches, FP32,
without optimizer updates; restore RNG afterward. Endpoint coefficient is 0.1
times median Dice+CE decoder-feature gradient RMS divided by median endpoint
decoder-feature gradient RMS. Completion coefficient uses the analogous ratio
at raw logits. The 0.1 target follows the existing calibration convention; its
suitability for this new task is NOT established. Fail if coefficient is nonfinite
or outside [1e-6,10], do not silently clip or tune. Freeze numerical coefficients
once per fold before branches. Ramp both auxiliary coefficients from 1/83 to
1 across the first continuation pass; thereafter constant. This ramp is an
optimization precaution, not a learned/readiness threshold. Head fit weight is
1 in its separate optimizer and has no effect on baseline AMP scaling/skips.

## Evaluation and selection locked before submission

Evaluate raw predictions only. Head endpoint MAE is diagnostic, never a selection
criterion. Inner metrics every epoch: ASSD (1 mm), union and class Dice, actual
thin overlap recall, thin voxel recall, FP rays/voxels, core recall (one 3D
binary erosion), true-voxel deletion/recovery relative to shared start and
matched control epoch, and endpoint errors/exclusion counts. Historical thin
recall definition is nonborder true span <=2; deletion audit additionally uses
one/two true voxels regardless of span. Keep these definitions explicit.

Control candidates must preserve shared-start Dice, both thin recalls, core
recall, FP rays and FP voxels (no worsening). Require zero newly deleted core
and count-thin true voxels, and total true deletions <= true recoveries.
Auxiliary candidates must satisfy these same guards against BOTH shared start
and the SAME-EPOCH control, and strictly improve ASSD against each. Select
minimum inner ASSD among eligible epochs; retain epoch 0 if none qualify.
These intentionally strict guards may reject every checkpoint. No post-hoc
relaxation. Fixed epoch-six results for all arms remain the main matched-update
comparison regardless of guard failure. Selected results are separately labeled
and may have different update counts; do not conflate them with fixed-epoch results.

Outer labels only compute reports after fixed training and inner selection;
they never change optimization, weights, readiness, selection or next fold's
settings. Report both fixed epoch-six and separately selected outcomes. Mask
banks used for paired deletion audits stay on cluster, with split/case records.
Only non-identifying aggregate JSON and job/test metadata may be downloaded.

## Integrity, storage and execution

Check dataset, split, original A checkpoints against recorded hashes, and frozen
source against provenance of job 666651. Record experiment/protocol hashes,
library version, argument settings and exact head parameter count. Resume checks
configuration and arm weights, restores paired state/RNG/counters, and skips
completed arms. Epoch snapshots are atomic. Training restarts from last complete
epoch after interruption, with deterministic matched data order. Never create a
second scheduler job to resume while the original is active.

Local tests: overlap rejects wrong position; all detachment paths; contextual
gradient masking; completion sign/gaps/empty groups; baseline optimizer parity;
zero completion arm equivalence; state/RNG restore; raw-only evaluation.
GPU smoke: two real preparation updates, exact weight/AdamW parity with pure
baseline, four-batch calibration, two active updates, paired checkpoint reload.
Run GPU smoke before submitting full training. Smoke is not experiment evidence.

Resource request: stud, one gpu:4g.40gb, 8 CPUs, 32 GiB RAM; smoke 20 minutes,
screen 4 hours. Estimated persistent experiment checkpoints approximately 4 GiB,
plus small mask banks; current free quota ~8.15 GiB. Require 2 GiB quota reserve
before each checkpoint write. No cleanup needed at lock time. If quota later
blocks, only user-authorized completed disposable artifacts may be considered
after provenance/scheduler/symlink checks; no automatic blanket cleanup.

# Direct annotated-contour supervision — locked pilot, 2026-09-23

The user authorized testing annotated contour supervision directly on backbone
segmentation probabilities. The minimal comparison is Dice/CE versus the same
Dice/CE plus a signed-distance boundary objective. No endpoint head, renderer,
reconstruction head, presence gate, image conditioning on GT, or neighbor-shape
loss is introduced. Raw backbone(image).argmax(1) remains inference.

This is a bounded one-fold continuation pilot, not training from scratch or an
exact reproduction of the published schedule. Motivation: Kervadec et al.,
Boundary loss for highly unbalanced segmentation, MIDL 2019,
https://proceedings.mlr.press/v102/kervadec19a.html .

## Data, initialization and matching

Use original fold1 A/best.pt from job666174 (backbone seed0), verifying its hash
and frozen source/data/split provenance from corrected experiment666967.
Historical fitting166 / inner42 cases; outer52 provide no training or evaluation
examples. All data are reused internal development data. No external/general
anatomical claim or independent-backbone-seed confirmation.

Both arms start from exactly the original A weights with identical new AdamW
states: lr3e-5, weight_decay1e-5, batch2, six epochs, 83 updates/epoch, exactly
498 backbone updates each. Original optimizer was pruned; optimizer restart is
explicit. There is no shared preparation pass because no new head needs it.
Continuation object seed9301; matched per-epoch order/RNG seed10301+epoch.
No early stopping, inner checkpoint selection, hyperparameter grid or outcome-
driven extension. Epoch6 is the primary comparison; inner trajectories are
descriptive and never control training. Old experiments/checkpoints stay frozen.

## Distance field and loss

For GT union foreground G=(label>0), compute on the historical isotropic 1mm
grid phi=EDT(not G)-EDT(G), distances to opposite-label voxel centers. Phi is
strictly negative on all foreground, strictly positive on all background.
In particular, a single foreground voxel has phi=-1; its nearest background
neighbor has phi=+1. This discrete convention is not an exact subvoxel contour
distance. Unlike conventions that subtract one from the inside EDT, it does
not zero the supervision on one-voxel-thick annotated anatomy. State this
choice explicitly; do not claim an exact reproduction of author implementation.

The boundary term is mean over cases/voxels of
  phi * (softmax(raw_logits)[class1] + softmax(raw_logits)[class2]).
It directly supervises the same probabilities used for segmentation. GT-derived
fields are detached training targets only; no target enters model.forward.
Signed loss values may be negative, which is expected. No clipping/absolute
value, bounding box, overlap eligibility, hard argmax or ray-filling target.
Real gaps and multi-run anatomy retain their actual voxel labels. Three-class
Dice/CE continues to supervise internal class division. Empty/full foreground
targets have no finite defined opposite-label distance here and cause a visible
failure rather than a fabricated map; the registered organ data should have both.

Cache SDFs in cluster RAM keyed by target content; never export them. No on-disk
image/mask cache. Control computes the same diagnostic boundary term but only
backpropagates Dice/CE. Preserve the historical baseline arithmetic expression.

## Coefficient locked using fitting data only

Before any updates, use exactly four shuffled fitting batches in FP32 under
seed9302. Compute raw-logit gradient RMS for Dice/CE and boundary loss. Fix
lambda=0.1*median(base_RMS)/median(boundary_RMS). Log the four norms and gradient
cosines; do not use those outcomes to choose another ratio. Require finite lambda
in [1e-6,100], fail otherwise. This is a magnitude convention, not established
optimal tuning. Restore original model weights/buffers after calibration.
Linearly ramp the boundary coefficient across the first 83 updates; hold fixed
for epochs2–6. No outcome/epoch readiness gate. Baseline is unchanged.

Use independent, freshly constructed optimizer/scaler objects per arm. AMP with
FP32 boundary softmax/reduction; abort on any backbone AMP skip. CUDA deterministic
warn-only mode retains original mean CE (cluster build lacks a strict deterministic
kernel); fixed seeds/cuDNN are used but universal bitwise determinism is not claimed.

## Evaluation and decision

Evaluate the original model and each epoch on the same inner42 cases, labels
used only after raw inference. Compare final6 versus fresh matched control and
versus original A. Report union/class Dice, ASSD, HD95, actual thin-overlap and
thin-voxel recall, FP rays/voxels, core/true recall, true deletions/recoveries and
core/thin deletions. Thin recall uses historical nonborder span<=2; deletion
audit uses 1–2 true voxels regardless of span. Predictions stay in cluster RAM.

Record strict preservation guards against original A and, for the boundary arm,
same-epoch control: no worse Dice/thin recalls/core recall/FP burdens, zero new
core/thin deletions, true deletions<=recoveries. Guards are reports, not checkpoint
selectors. A safe gain also requires lower ASSD. Report partial improvements and
tradeoffs honestly; failed guards alone do not imply absent geometric learning.
No clinical or new-cohort claim; no automatic model promotion.

## Verification, resources and storage

Unit tests: signed EDT including thin voxels, correct direct logit gradient
signs inside/outside, distance weighting, preservation of GT gaps, detached
targets/class-union symmetry, caching and exact zero-weight AdamW parity.
GPU smoke: four fitting calibration batches, two pure baseline updates versus
two zero-coefficient updates with exact weight/optimizer/scaler equality; two
active boundary updates; finite weights and checkpoint roundtrip. Smoke outcomes
are execution checks, not scientific evidence or a tuning set.

Full run: stud, one gpu:4g.40gb, eight CPUs, 32GiB, one hour. Smoke 15 minutes.
Quota was about2.85GiB free; unchanged 2GiB reserve before checkpoint writes.
Store one ~70MB smoke roundtrip checkpoint and only two final model checkpoints
(no optimizer snapshots); peak includes one temporary model file, around280MB
logical, conservatively560MB quota allocation. No cleanup required/planned.
Epoch histories preserve progress, but this job has no optimizer-state resume.
Failure is reported without silent relaunch or schedule change. No duplicate jobs.

Only non-identifying aggregate results/provenance/job metadata may be downloaded
under standing authorization. Images, masks, distance maps, split/case identifiers,
individual records and checkpoints remain on cluster. Monitor through completion;
verify exit0, both498-update arms, hashes and provenance, then pause monitoring.

Protocol evidence: overfit_loss_flow_20260923_01a0cd/OVERFIT_LOSS_FLOW_PROTOCOL_20260923.md
# Frozen-head loss, activation and gradient audit

Written before execution. Audit the 24 final heads of job 666786 on exactly
their four fitting cases per fold (seven distinct cases across folds). No
training, checkpoint reselection, inner or outer evaluation.

Decompose the original case/group-balanced interval objective exactly into six
disjoint groups: initially missed feasible thin rays, initially missed infeasible
thin rays, initially overlapping thin rays, other true rays, hard-empty rays,
and other empty rays. Preserve original four-group normalization; splitting a
group for reporting must not increase its loss weight. Split each contribution
into lower hinge, upper hinge, tie and infeasible-zero terms. Assert the losses
and parameter gradients sum back to the unchanged original objective. Compare
paired state-input versus original-input contributions and zero-correction loss.

For currently unrescued feasible thin rays, report distance in residual logits
to the safe rescue lower bound, allowed interval width and the derivative of the
bounded tanh correction. Report fractions of gaps within .01,.1,.25,.5,1,2 logits.
These label-defined measurements are retrospective diagnostics, not features.

Report actual masks for unchanged learned corrections and fixed +0.25/+0.5-logit
increments, clipped to the original domain. Also evaluate a explicitly
non-deployable oracle: increase only currently unrescued feasible true thin rays
to their target lower bound, leaving every other learned correction unchanged.
Assert that this oracle adds no FP voxel or true deletion relative to the learned
mask. It quantifies available selective rescue, not a deployable result or the
share of total ASSD attributable to thin rays. No ASSD is recomputed.

At each saved head, compute gradients for each weighted group contribution,
their norms and pairwise cosines. Compute derivatives of the mean correction
on currently unrescued feasible thin rays, hard-empty rays and already-overlapping
thin rays, pooling each receiver's rays over the four cases. Report the signed
first-order response to minus the total gradient normalized to unit parameter
L2 norm, and each loss group's additive contribution to that same direction.
Positive response means increased mean correction. Direct loss gradients with
respect to correction are reported separately. This is a local SGD diagnostic,
not an AdamW update, historical causal reconstruction or training forecast.
Saved optimizer states are not available and no parameter update is performed.

Discriminating findings:

- Concentrated loss reduction on feasible missed thin rays supports improvement
  on the intended target, but must be checked against actual threshold crossings.
- Small gaps with unsaturated correction suggest threshold placement is an
  actionable issue; large gaps refute a merely numerical near-threshold account.
- Opposing group gradients and adverse shared-parameter response despite the
  desired direct output signal support local gradient interference.
- Saturation, zero gradients or missing signal suggest different mechanisms.
  None alone establishes the cause of earlier training failures.

Report all heads, paired fold/seed differences and heterogeneous signs. Verify
source/input/checkpoint hashes and reproduce saved fitting losses. Export only
non-identifying aggregates under the user's authorization for current and future
aggregate reports in this investigation. Keep images and individual case records
on the cluster; preserve every saved model.

Protocol evidence: medsam3_discarded_pilots.md
# Superseded MedSAM3 inference-refinement pilots (28 September 2026)

Archived at the user's request before deleting generated experiment artifacts.
These experiments applied bands/edge as new mask-free **post-inference
refinements**, which did not answer the intended training-loss question.

Zero-shot job 673230, hippocampus_017: baseline Dice 0.0086180980;
+bands 0.0079565302; +bands+edge 0.0079634845.

Five-shot job 673282 used training volumes 011, 056, 146, 319, 363 (prefix
hippocampus_), seed 42, final LoRA after 200 AdamW updates, four random slices
per update, LR 5e-5 with 20-update warmup/cosine decay to 5e-6. The base model
remained frozen. Whole-hippocampus binary 3D Dice on separate validation volumes:

| Case | Zero-shot | Five-shot | + bands | + bands + edge |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| hippocampus_017 | 0.008618 | 0.868163 | 0.853706 | 0.855359 |
| hippocampus_019 | 0.000514 | 0.836421 | 0.839829 | 0.840205 |
| hippocampus_033 | 0.001736 | 0.881514 | 0.859003 | 0.860000 |
| hippocampus_035 | 0.003947 | 0.873124 | 0.873990 | 0.875187 |
| hippocampus_037 | 0.008629 | 0.836256 | 0.812246 | 0.812439 |
| Mean | 0.004689 | 0.859096 | 0.847755 | 0.848638 |

Both jobs completed; saved-mask Dice and grid/hash checks passed. The original
case's repeated zero-shot output was identical. Few-shot adaptation helped,
while post-inference constraints lowered mean Dice. These results do not test
supervised constraints during fine-tuning. The old predictions, trained adapter,
plots, logs, result archives and detailed run records were authorized for
removal. Original datasets, downloaded SAM3/medical weights, reusable source
code and shared runtime are retained for the corrected training experiment.
